config.title: Production Node.js

intro.title: Production Node.js
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, production-ready Node.js server that handles HTTP requests and logs important events. You'll learn the core concept of structuring a Node.js application for reliability and monitoring in a live environment. The main technologies involved include the built-in 'http' module for creating a server, the 'fs' module for file operations, and environment variables for configuration. By the end, you'll understand how to set up a basic production server with error handling and logging to prepare your Node.js apps for real-world use.
intro.usecase: Production Node.js skills are essential for building scalable backend services that power real-world applications like e-commerce platforms, social media APIs, and financial systems. Developers use these techniques to create robust RESTful APIs that handle thousands of concurrent requests, such as payment processing endpoints for online stores or real-time chat servers. These production-ready patterns ensure applications remain performant during traffic spikes, maintain data integrity with proper error handling, and provide reliable uptime through health monitoring and logging. Mastering these concepts allows you to deploy Node.js applications that can scale from small startups to enterprise-level systems.

objectives: Configure environment variables for different deployment stages
Implement structured logging with appropriate severity levels
Construct error handling middleware for production applications
Initialize and configure process monitoring tools
Integrate health check endpoints into Node.js applications
Apply performance optimization techniques for production environments
Manipulate application configuration based on deployment context

steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the required Node.js modules: http for creating servers, fs for file system operations, and path for handling file paths.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. You'll need three separate require statements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have three require statements importing the http, fs, and path modules.
successCriteria: The http, fs, and path modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but you need all three: http, fs, and path.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports don't match what's needed. You need to import http, fs, and path modules using require().

steps.title: Create the main server file structure
steps.instruction: Create a basic Node.js server file structure by declaring a constant named 'server' and assigning it the result of calling the 'http.createServer()' method.
steps.hint: Use 'const server = http.createServer();' to create an HTTP server instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating a server instance
const server = http.createServer();
steps.seedCode:
// Import required Node.js modules here

const server = http.createServer();
steps.expectedOutcome: A constant named 'server' is declared and assigned an HTTP server instance created with 'http.createServer()'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using 'const server = http.createServer();' exactly as shown.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to create a constant named 'server' and assign it the result of 'http.createServer()'.

steps.title: Initialize the HTTP server
steps.instruction: Create an HTTP server instance using the http module's createServer method and assign it to a constant named 'server'.
steps.hint: Use the createServer method from the http module you imported earlier. Assign the result to a constant variable named 'server'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a server instance
const server = http.createServer();
steps.seedCode:
// Import required Node.js modules here

const server = http.createServer();
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTTP server instance is created and assigned to the 'server' constant.
successCriteria: The server constant is declared and assigned the result of http.createServer()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using http.createServer() and assigning it to a constant named 'server'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server instance wasn't created correctly. Use http.createServer() and assign it to a constant named 'server'.

steps.title: Define server request handling logic
steps.instruction: Add a callback function to the createServer method that handles incoming HTTP requests and responses.
steps.hint: The createServer method accepts a callback function with request and response parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now have a request handler callback function ready to process incoming requests.
successCriteria: A callback function with req and res parameters is added to createServer.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a callback function with both req and res parameters to createServer.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request handler callback is missing or incomplete. Add a function with req and res parameters to createServer.

steps.title: Add basic routing for the home page
steps.instruction: Inside the request handler, add an if statement to check if the request URL is the root path ('/') and respond with a welcome message.
steps.hint: Use req.url to get the request URL and res.writeHead() with status 200 and Content-Type header, then res.end() to send the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now respond to requests to the root URL with a plain text welcome message.
successCriteria: An if statement checks req.url === '/' and responds with status 200, Content-Type header, and a welcome message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented basic routing for the home page.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to include the status code, header, and response body.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the if condition and response methods. The server should handle the root path specifically.

steps.title: Add error handling for 404 routes
steps.instruction: Add an else clause after your existing if statement to handle all other routes with a 404 response.
steps.hint: After your existing if block, add an else block that sets the response status to 404 and sends a 'Not Found' message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now respond with a 404 status and message for any route other than '/'.
successCriteria: An else clause is added after the if statement that sets status 404 and sends a 'Not Found' message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your else clause properly sets the status code and sends a response.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding an else clause after your if statement to handle all other routes with a 404 response.

steps.title: Create a static file serving function
steps.instruction: Create a helper function named 'serveStaticFile' that takes 'res', 'filePath', and 'contentType' as parameters and serves static files with proper headers and error handling.
steps.hint: Define a function that sets the Content-Type header, reads the file using fs.readFile, and sends the file content or an error response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'serveStaticFile' is defined with parameters for response, file path, and content type, including file reading and error handling logic.
successCriteria: The serveStaticFile function is created with proper parameters, sets Content-Type header, reads the file using fs.readFile, and handles errors with a 500 status response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it includes all parameters (res, filePath, contentType), sets the Content-Type header, reads the file with fs.readFile, and handles errors with a 500 response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The serveStaticFile function is missing or incorrect. Create a function named 'serveStaticFile' that takes res, filePath, and contentType parameters, sets headers, reads the file, and handles errors.

steps.title: Integrate static file serving into routing
steps.instruction: Inside the request handling logic, add an else-if condition to check if the request URL starts with '/static/' and call the serveStaticFile function for those requests.
steps.hint: Use req.url.startsWith('/static/') to identify static file requests, then call serveStaticFile(req.url, res) to serve the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will now handle requests to '/static/' URLs by serving static files through the serveStaticFile function.
successCriteria: An else-if condition is added that checks if req.url starts with '/static/' and calls serveStaticFile(req.url, res).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some routing logic, but make sure to check for '/static/' URLs and call serveStaticFile.
steps.feedbackWrong: The static file serving isn't properly integrated. Check if you added the else-if condition and called serveStaticFile.

steps.title: Add environment configuration
steps.instruction: Read the PORT environment variable and use it to set the server's listening port, defaulting to 3000 if not set.
steps.hint: Use process.env.PORT to access the environment variable. Provide a fallback value with the logical OR operator.
steps.analogousExample:
// Reading environment variable with fallback
const port = process.env.PORT || 3000;
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to use a port from the environment, making it production-ready.
successCriteria: The code reads process.env.PORT and provides a default fallback value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to read the PORT environment variable and provide a default fallback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The environment configuration is missing or incorrect. Use process.env.PORT with a fallback value.

steps.title: Add request logging middleware
steps.instruction: Create a function named logRequest that takes request and response objects as parameters and logs the request method, URL, and current timestamp to the console.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses console.log to output the request details. You can get the current timestamp with new Date().toISOString().
steps.expectedOutcome: A logRequest function is defined that will log request details when called.
successCriteria: The logRequest function exists, takes req and res parameters, and logs method, URL, and timestamp to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function logs the request method, URL, and a timestamp.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logRequest function isn't defined correctly. Create a function that logs request details.

steps.title: Start the server with proper error handling
steps.instruction: Add server.listen() after the server creation to start the server on port 3000, include error handling for the listen operation, and log a success message when the server starts.
steps.hint: Use server.listen() with the port number, and provide a callback function to handle any errors and log a success message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start listening on port 3000, with error handling for the listen operation and a success message logged to the console.
successCriteria: server.listen() is called with port 3000, includes error handling, and logs a success message when the server starts.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added server.listen(), but make sure to include error handling and log a success message when the server starts.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started correctly. Ensure you call server.listen() with port 3000, handle errors, and log a success message.

steps.title: Test the production server
steps.instruction: Start the server by adding the server.listen() method call with proper error handling and a success message.
steps.hint: Call server.listen() with the port from your environment configuration and add callback functions for error handling and the success message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start successfully and be ready to handle requests on the configured port.
successCriteria: server.listen() is called with the port from environment configuration, includes error handling with .on('error'), and logs a success message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added server.listen() but might be missing error handling or the success message. Check the analogous example.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server.listen() method is not properly implemented. Review how to start a server with error handling.
